The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission has warned electricity distribution companies against charging consumers for meters supplied under the N30bn third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund, insisting that the equipment and installation must be free. The commission said the intervention covers all 11 electricity distribution companies and targets all remaining unmetered Band A customers, while accelerating meter deployment to Band B customers. In Order No. NERC/2026/121 on Tranche C of the Meter Acquisition Fund, the regulator directed DisCos to ensure that customers do not pay for meters provided under the programme. NERC also warned that distribution companies would face sanctions where their actions or failure to meet stipulated obligations delay meter installation. The regulator directed that all meters supplied under the scheme must carry the name of the relevant DisCo, the MAF tranche and the inscription, ‘NOT FOR SALE’. The commission further stated that where a DisCo decides to relocate an existing customer’s meter connection point to a pole or high wall to protect its revenue, the company must bear the cost. It stated, “Where a DisCo elects to relocate an existing customer’s connection point to a pole or high wall to ensure revenue protection, such DisCo shall bear the relocation cost.” NERC also prescribed penalties for distribution companies whose failure to provide network clearance or accurate customer information delays installations. The commission fixed 31 May 2027 as the deadline for completing installations under the third tranche. It directed consumers who are asked to pay for meters under the programme to complain to their distribution companies before escalating unresolved cases to NERC Forum Offices or their respective State Electricity Regulatory Commissions. The N30bn fund is expected to support the metering of customers across the 11 DisCos, with allocations based on the distribution companies’ respective requirements. NERC said the order was intended to ensure transparent implementation, accountability and wider access to electricity meters. “Your meter and its installation are free. Do not pay anyone for it. Look for the sticker: your DisCo’s name, the MAF tranche and ‘NOT FOR SALE’. “If your DisCo moves your existing meter to secure its network, the DisCo pays. Not you. DisCos face sanctions where their default delays installation. All installations must be completed on or before 31 May 2027. “Asked to pay? Complain to your DisCo first, then escalate to the NERC Forum Office or your State Electricity Regulatory Commission,” NERC said in a notice on its social media handles.
